title: Parasitic Method Objects (Indirection Astronautics)
pattern: Instantiating a specialized struct ("Method Object") for a trivial, non-complex computation simply to avoid passing local variables as arguments.
why_bad: Introduces severe indirection and memory/lifetime management overhead (such as mutable references inside short-lived objects) to perform simple operations. It creates a high number of single-use structural ghosts that waste developer time to read and maintain.
detection: Identify structs designed to wrap a single method invocation, where all fields are references or local inputs, and the struct's lifecycle ends immediately after calling its executor method.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Highly complex algorithms with 20+ interacting variables that cannot be cleanly refactored via standard parameter lists.
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 6, "Replace Method with Method Object" (p. 151).
